channel.title: Hacker News posts on daily.dev
channel.description: Hacker News is a community-driven platform for sharing and discussing technology news, startups, and programming-related topics. Through user submissions and comments, Hacker News offers insights into emerging technology trends, industry developments, and entrepreneurial ventures. Readers can participate in discussions, share their insights, and stay informed about the latest advancements in technology and innovation. - Powered by RSSHub

item.title: Why do I run FreeBSD for my home servers.
item.description: Examines the reasons for choosing FreeBSD for home servers, including its stability, security features, and ZFS file system support. Offers insight into its performance, ease of use, and how it handles server tasks efficiently.

item.title: Notes on the Pentium's microcode circuitry
item.description: Microcode is an additional layer of software embedded in processors, such as the Pentium, to execute machine instructions through a series of simpler micro-instructions. The Pentium’s microcode ROM, responsible for storing these micro-instructions, is a complex structure with several thousand micro-instructions that control the processor’s functions. The design includes various levels of metal wiring to optimize performance and different techniques to improve testing accuracy and mitigate errors.

item.title: JEP draft: Prepare to Make Final Mean Final
item.description: The proposed Java Enhancement Proposal (JEP) aims to issue warnings about the use of deep reflection to change final fields in Java. This sets the stage for a future release where the immutability of final fields will be enforced to improve program safety and performance. Developers will need to explicitly enable the ability to mutate final fields at startup if required. This aligns final fields in regular classes with those in record classes and continues to support serialization libraries.

item.title: Family Plan
item.description: Kagi's Family Plan aims to provide a safe and educational search experience for families, with special emphasis on children. It offers ad-free browsing, parental controls, kid-friendly content filters, personalized search results, and new features like AI-powered quick answers and customizable search lenses. The plan is affordable and designed to respect family privacy.

item.title: Honey has now lost 4 million Chrome users after shady tactics were revealed
item.description: Honey, a popular Chrome extension owned by PayPal known for finding coupon codes, has lost around 4 million users. This decline follows a viral video in December 2024 that exposed the extension for dishonest use of affiliate codes. Despite updates to comply with new Chrome policies, which restrict such practices, Honey has not managed to regain its peak user base of 20 million.

item.title: France fines Apple €150M for “excessive” pop-ups that let users reject tracking
item.description: France's competition regulator fined Apple €150 million, citing the excessive complexity of the pop-up messages used to obtain user consent for tracking through third-party applications. The App Tracking Transparency (ATT) framework reportedly puts small publishers at a disadvantage, as they rely on third-party data for advertisement revenue. The French agency claims Apple's implementation distorts competition and complicates the use of third-party apps on iOS devices.

item.title: MLB says Yankees’ new Torpedo Bats are legal and likely coming to a dugout near you but are we sure this is what we want?
item.description: The Yankees have introduced a new 'torpedo bat' designed by MIT physicist Lenny, aimed at increasing the contact area for hitters. The bat proved effective, as the Yankees hit a record number of home runs in a game. MLB has deemed the bat legal, despite its unconventional design. The innovation raises questions about the future of bat technology and its impact on the game.

item.title: Offline Sync Public Beta
item.description: Turso Offline Sync is now in public beta, allowing applications to function seamlessly offline by syncing local database operations once connectivity is restored. This feature enhances the performance and resilience of applications, making them responsive to network failures. Currently, the beta supports TypeScript and Rust, with potential for future enhancements in different environments like in-browser and Expo.

item.title: Browsercraft
item.description: Browsercraft allows the unmodified version of Minecraft to run in browsers using CheerpJ, a Java runtime for modern browsers. This is achieved by running an older version (1.2.5) of Minecraft and LWJGL entirely in the browser. The project is still a work-in-progress with some features like audio not yet supported. Programmers are encouraged to contribute to the project.

item.title: Sergey's Blog
item.description: AI systems need to focus on reliability and predictability over flashy capabilities. Complex, opaque AI agents can lead to user frustration and distrust. Simple, comprehensible interfaces are preferred, with emphasis on minimizing variance and focusing on well-understood tasks. Good UX design should prevent mistakes and ensure transparency, which helps in building user trust.
